sources.history: Archived CPI news releases available back to 1994 on the BLS site
sources.publication_semantics: Archived CPI releases preserve the release text and state the embargo/release timestamp; current 2026 CPI releases are published at 08:30 America/New_York.
notes: Use archived release values, not the current API value, when reconstructing historical first-known inflation evidence.
Seasonally adjusted indexes can be revised; release snapshots must remain versioned rather than overwritten.

sources.provider: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.history: Long historical H.15 series available directly from the Board; daily H.15 release is posted at 16:15 America/New_York.
sources.publication_semantics: Each daily H.15 release contains recent effective federal funds and Treasury constant-maturity observations; Board calendar/release pages provide publication timing.
notes: Current downloadable history can reflect later corrections; strict retrospective use requires an archived release copy or other original-vintage proof.
Prospective collection may store each actual release from ingestion forward.

sources.history: Daily par yield curve archive available from 1990 onward; real yield curve archive from 2003 onward.
sources.publication_semantics: Treasury states that the nominal par curve uses indicative market quotations obtained around 15:30 America/New_York; downloadable daily CSV/XML archives are available.
notes: Current historical archive does not by itself prove the original unrevised vintage of every historical day.
Use actual ingestion time prospectively unless a release-time archive proves earlier availability.

sources.history: ECB SDMX data portal provides long historical series; euro-area yield curves are available daily from 2004-09-06.
sources.publication_semantics: ECB euro-area yield curves are published daily at noon CET; ECB reference FX rates are normally updated around 16:00 CET after the 14:15 concertation procedure.
notes: Third-party data remain excluded from the ECB free-reuse rule unless separately cleared.
Current historical series may incorporate revisions; retrospective original-vintage use must be separately proven.

sources.history: Long daily spot-price histories exist for WTI, Brent and Henry Hub natural gas.
sources.publication_semantics: EIA publishes dated energy observations and machine-readable API data; the API terms explicitly allow development of services that retrieve, display and analyze EIA data.
notes: Current historical series can contain later corrections; strict historical PIT should use archived release evidence where available or remain latest-vintage research only.
Prospective snapshots can be made strict PIT from actual ingestion forward.

sources.history: Monthly and annual commodity-price history plus monthly Pink Sheet publications.
sources.publication_semantics: Monthly Pink Sheet documents carry document/web publication timestamps and historical monthly workbooks are published alongside them.
notes: World Bank-produced open datasets default to CC BY 4.0, but dataset-specific metadata must be checked before activation.
Monthly frequency is slower than EIA for oil/gas but may provide one openly reusable family for gold, silver and copper if archive validation passes.

sources.history: IMF Primary Commodity Prices statistical data are available through IMF data services/APIs.
sources.publication_semantics: IMF statistical data may be downloaded, extracted, copied, transformed and distributed with attribution, subject to IMF data terms and any third-party conditions.
notes: Do not use as historical PIT evidence until original publication/vintage semantics are proven.
Keep as a fallback to World Bank/EIA rather than adding another redundant commodity source immediately.

sources.history: Annual U.S. uranium purchase and contract-price reports are available back for decades.
sources.publication_semantics: Annual report release dates and later revision notices are explicit.
notes: Useful as slow structural uranium context, not as a substitute for a timely uranium spot/market series.
Free timely uranium spot benchmarks remain a source gap.

explicit_source_gaps.uranium: No free timely spot benchmark with cleared licensing and proven strict historical PIT has been accepted; EIA annual data are too slow for the primary context role.
explicit_source_gaps.lithium: No clean open standardized lithium price series has been accepted. World Bank documentation explicitly notes that its GEM/Pink Sheet commodity dataset does not contain lithium price data and uses S&P Global Market Intelligence for lithium in another methodology context.

blocked_sources.reason: Current FRED terms prohibit API use in connection with software/system development and prohibit storing/caching/archiving FRED content; Scanner_vNext requires both system use and persisted vintages.
